synthesis: The narrow search reported two hits but returned no records, so nothing has been inspected. Three leads recalled from memory are listed for checking: an A3 report from a surgical unit, a questionnaire study of nurses' barriers, and a practice guide on pairing awakening and breathing trials. A broader search is needed before any certainty can be stated.

items.title: A3 problem solving to improve spontaneous awakening trial completion in a surgical intensive care unit
items.keyFindings: An A3 led by bedside nurses was followed by a rise in completed awakening trials over six months in one surgical unit.
items.notes: Recalled as a lead; one of the two hits the provider did not serve may be this report.

items.title: Barriers to daily sedation interruption reported by critical care nurses: a multicentre questionnaire study
items.authors: Mistry-Oduya L, Kaplan-Reyes D, Sorensen-Iwu T
items.source: Journal of Critical Care Nursing Practice
items.keyFindings: Nurses most often cited fear of agitation and self-extubation, workload before rounds and unclear authority to stop sedation.
items.limitations: Recalled lead; self-report; method quality not stated.
items.notes: Recalled as a lead; not retrieved.

items.title: Paired awakening and breathing trials in routine practice: a practice guide
items.keyFindings: Recommends a fixed morning time for paired awakening and breathing trials agreed between nursing and respiratory therapy.
items.limitations: Recalled lead; consensus guide; evidence base not described.

summary: Three unchecked leads; certainty left unassessed; a broader search is needed.
